title: A trusted machine's own bundle (ship-fleet machine-bundle NAME, version 1)
description: Printed on stdout by `ship-fleet machine-bundle NAME` on the FleetLedger computer, for the trusted machine NAME, which asks for it over ssh to keep its SSH setup current (its certificate, its known_hosts and SSH config, its hc machines, and a file of the fleet's Ships). Data: the machine checks every field and writes its files from templates of its own. The one exception, refresher, is read only by the first-install line a person pastes; the refresher never reads it. Only the Ships NAME's scope reaches are listed. A refusal prints nothing on stdout. See contracts/ship-fleet.md.

machine.description: The trusted machine this bundle is for (its name in ships.toml).

certificate.description: The machine's user certificate, for its own key. A new one is signed only once the current one is past half its life; otherwise the current one comes again.

line.description: The certificate, as a <machine>-cert.pub file holds it. null: FleetLedger has none that is still valid and could not sign one (not_renewed says why).

valid_before.description: When line lapses; null with line.

oneOf.description: A new certificate was due and was not signed. line is the current one while it is still valid, else null. The machine asks again later; nothing is signed without the vault unlocked.

code.description: vault-locked: FleetLedger's vault is locked (ship-fleet unlock). sign-failed: the CA could not sign (why).

scope.description: Which Ships the machine may reach (ships.toml machine.<name>.scope).

logins.description: What its certificate logs in as on those Ships.

user.description: The login its SSH config uses on every Ship: agent when it may log in as the agent, else your own login.

known_hosts.description: The lines of its known_hosts for Ships: one @cert-authority line naming every name of every Ship listed (none while no Ship is), then an @revoked line per host key the CA revoked.

oneOf.description: FleetLedger's own VM (ships.toml fleet.self), so the machine can keep its pin of the computer it asks.

known_hosts.description: Its host key, as a known_hosts line naming every name it is reached by.

fleetledger.description: null when FleetLedger does not run on a VM of its own that it recorded (ship-fleet appliance).

ships.description: Every Ship the machine's scope reaches, by name; none outside it.

name.description: Its SSH Host alias and hc machine name.

tags.description: Its tags (defaults.tags when it has none of its own).

runtime.description: From its last status: core (herdr-core: hc attaches) or herdr (classic: herdr --remote). core when not fetched yet, as a new Ship runs.

host_names.description: What to put as its HostName. Both are among the names its host certificate names.

lan.description: The first of its names other than the overlay one that resolves on the FleetLedger computer, else the first of them.

overlay.description: Its overlay name, which works off the LAN; null when it is not on the overlay.

host_certificate.description: Its last status shows a host certificate. Without one, ssh to it fails the CA check until ship-fleet ca sign.

refresher.description: The refresher script (FleetLedger's fleetledger/refresher/refresh.sh), base64. Only the first-install line ship-fleet trust prints decodes it, once, when a person pastes that line on the machine; the refresher never reads this field and never replaces itself, so a refresh applies data only. Absent from a FleetLedger older than the refresher.

on.description: true: after days without asking, the machine is refused its bundle until allowed again (ship-fleet trust NAME --allow-again). false: it stays trusted until untrusted.

timestamp.description: UTC, RFC 3339, with a Z suffix.
